messages:
sara: Heads-up — multiple customers hitting repeated 5xx / timeouts from the hosted text-generation endpoint since ~08:12 UTC. Primary symptom: long tail of 504s and occasional 500s with the body 'gateway timeout' or 'internal server error'. Customers reporting correlation IDs in request headers. Sam, can you paste a repro and the customer's request IDs?

sam-cs: Pasting payload from ACME support ticket (customer says ~08:14 UTC):

```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-v1","input":"Summarize quarterly plan","max_tokens":200}'
```
Response (sample):

```
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: rq_0a1b2c3d4e
{ "error": "gateway timeout" }
```
Customer also provided server-side trace id: trace=acme-54321. They say toggling retries doesn't help, and it started ~after 08:10 UTC.

opsbot: :rotating_light: Alert — prefix-cache-service (prefix-cacher-prod) error-rate spike detected at 08:11 UTC: 520 errors/min, avg latency 780ms. Redis pool errors: connection-timeout and i/o timeout. Auto-failover attempted. Monitoring link: https://metrics.redwood.ai/alert/pc-123

miguel: I'm oncall and looking. Initial read: our prefix-cacher depends on Redis (cache for KV/prefix lookups). If Redis is slow or failing, prefix-cacher is blocking requests which the gateway treats as upstream failure => 5xx/timeouts. I'm SSHing into prefix-cacher logs now.

miguel: Log snippet from prefix-cacher at 08:12:23:

```
2026-03-15T08:12:23Z ERROR prefix_lookup.go:142 cache.Read failed: redis: ReadTimeout (i/o timeout) conn=10.4.2.11:6379
2026-03-15T08:12:23Z WARN request_handler.go:87 upstream latency=823ms route=/v1/generate req=rq_0a1b2c3d4e
2026-03-15T08:12:24Z ERROR pool.go:98 getConn: dial tcp 10.4.2.11:6379: i/o timeout
```
So Redis nodes are intermittently unreachable / slow. I can trigger a quick mitigation: set route-level prefix_cache=false for impacted routes or toggle an emergency bypass that skips prefix lookups.

lee: Runtime note — prefix lookups are on the critical path for token streaming setup (we check prefix/KV for cached KV cache and next-token hints). When prefix-cacher blocks, the request stalls and the gateway times out. Even fallback model variants still hit prefix-cacher. So disabling prefix lookups for the hot routes should reduce 5xx immediately.

sara: Are there a small number of high-traffic customers causing thrashing? Any sign of sudden keyspace scan or hot keys?

miguel: Early sign: large spike in prefix-miss writes from a ML experiment tenant, plus a few spikes of multi-get storms. Redis CPU low, but net I/O high and many TIME_WAIT sockets. Looks like client connection pool exhaustion.

lee: Quick workaround (safe): apply per-customer route override to bypass prefix cache. Example API config change (do not share keys publicly):

```bash
# disable prefix cache on route id route-acme-001
curl -X PATCH https://console.redwood.ai/api/routes/route-acme-001 -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin_token' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"prefix_cache": false, "note":"emergency bypass - redis outage 2026-03-15"}'
```
This should make the request path skip prefix-cacher and avoid the Redis dependency. Recommend toggling for the top 10 heavy routes first.

sam-cs: I can apply the bypass for ACME and two other impacted customers now. Any guidance for asking customers to retry?

miguel: Yes, apply bypass, then ask customers to retry once; their previous requests likely timed out and won't be retried automatically. Also, we can temporarily bump prefix-cacher connection timeout and pool size as a short-term mitigation:

```
# runtime config change (ops only)
prefix_cacher.conn_timeout = 800ms -> 1500ms
prefix_cacher.max_pool = 200 -> 400
```

This buys time while we stabilize Redis. I'll coordinate a Redis failover / replace unhealthy node.

anna: From billing — can we get the list of affected customers and time window so we can prepare credits? Sam, please collect corp_ids and impacted request counts.

sam-cs: Will do. For ACME we have ~120 failing requests between 08:10-08:20 UTC. Adding their corp id to the ticket.

opsbot: Update — Redis cluster node redis-10-4-2-11 unreachable, failover initiated at 08:15 UTC. Incident runbook step 3 triggered by oncall.

miguel: I restarted the prefix-cacher pods on the two most-loaded zones to force new connections and drop stuck sockets. After restart, error-rate dropped from 520/min to 18/min in the next 90s. I opened a ticket for the infra team to investigate the underlying Redis network egress flaps.

lee: Observability notes — we should add a defensive timeout in the gateway: if prefix-cacher latency > 300ms, route should skip synchronous prefix checks and mark for async post-process. That will prevent the gateway from blocking on cache dependency. Filed RFC: #rfc/async-prefix-fallback.

miguel: Confirmed: Redis failover completed at 08:21 UTC, cluster healthy metrics show 95th latency back to normal. Rolling restart and the connection pool change reduced tail latency. Monitoring shows 5xxs dropped to baseline by 08:24 UTC.

sara: Great. Sam — let customers know we performed an emergency bypass for their routes and the underlying Redis cluster had a transient network failure; service recovered after failover and prefix-cacher restarts. Apologize and offer one day's service credit; Anna to finalize.

sam-cs: Noted. Messaging draft: "We identified a transient issue in our cache dependency that caused timeouts. We applied a temporary bypass and recovered service; we're doing a deeper postmortem and will credit impacted requests." Will send per-customer notes with request IDs.

anna: I'll prepare credit drafts and hold until we have list of impacted corp_ids from Sam.

opsbot: Incident resolved (auto): prefix-cacher error-rate < 1/min for 10m and Redis cluster stable. Incident window 08:10–08:24 UTC.

miguel: Closing steps: 1) revert emergency prefix bypass after 24h if stable; 2) increase connection pool defaults; 3) infra to investigate host-level network flaps; 4) follow-up postmortem with timeline and action items.

lee: I'll add an integration test that simulates Redis timeouts and ensures the gateway falls back smoothly. Putting it on the sprint.

sara: Thanks all. Keeping thread open until postmortem. :white_check_mark:
